summary: A scholar of sinology, japanology, and Buddhist studies, Waley was educated at King's College, Cambridge, and studied under Gustav Haloun, Laurence Binyon, and Hidetsugu Yagi. He served at the British Museum (1913–1929) and SOAS (1948).

An Indologist, Ryder studied at Harvard (A.B.), Berlin, and Leipzig (Ph.D.), working under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He taught Sanskrit at Harvard (1902–1906) before serving as professor at UC Berkeley (~1906–1938).
Educated at Wellington College and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1869–1873), Verrall taught Robert Alexander Neil.

An Indologist and religious studies scholar, Dhand studied at the University of Calgary and McGill University. Around 2000, she became an Associate Professor in the Department for the Study of Religion at the University of Toronto.
Active in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies, Haldar studied under Kedarnath Ojha and Girindrasekhar Bose. She held a teaching post at Patna University.

An Indologist, Jani completed his Ph.D. at the University of Mumbai under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt and also studied under M. V. Upadhyay. He served as Senior Lecturer and later director (1967–1981) at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda.
Gupta studied under Stephen Cook and Alasdair Urquhart.

A scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, Sharma earned degrees from Allahabad, Syracuse, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard. He held posts at Queensland (1976), Sydney (1980), McGill (1994), and Harvard (~2004).

A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, Tilakaratne was Professor and Head at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, University of Kelaniya. He is attested as an Emeritus Professor there and Foreign Adjunct Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 2026.
A Buddhist studies scholar, Kamiya earned an M.A. from Komazawa University (attested 1973). In 1978, he is attested as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School.

A scholar of Tibetology, Balikci received his PhD from Columbia University in 1956. He worked at the Musée d'ethnographie de Neuchâtel, the Canadian Museum of History, the National Museum of Canada, and the University of Montreal (1963–1993).

A scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, Chatterjee earned his degrees at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti. He taught at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University (1950–1963) and BHU (1947–1950, 1963–1985).
A scholar of philosophy and Indology, Malhotra studied at the East-West Center (~1964–1969) and founded the State University of New York at Oneonta.

An Indologist, linguist, and philosopher, Aklujkar studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, among others. He was appointed to the Department of Asian Studies at the University of British Columbia (1969–2006).

A linguist and Indologist, Kelkar studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Cornell University. He held posts at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University, Pune University, and Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1967–1989).

An Indologist, Mukherjee studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He served at the Calcutta High Court (1904), led The Asiatic Society (~1907–1915), and served as President of the University of Calcutta (1906–1914, 1921–1923).

An Indologist and historian, Chatterjee completed his Ph.D. at the University of Calcutta under D. Mukherjee in 1967. He served as a Senior Research Fellow there (attested 1970) and was a lecturer in English at Jangipur College.

An Indologist and linguist, Parpola studied under Pentti Aalto, R. Panneerselvam, and P. R. Subramanian. He held positions at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies (1968), the Academy of Finland, and was a professor at the University of Helsinki (~1982–2004).
An archaeologist, Goodwin studied at St. John's College, Selwyn College, and SOAS. He took up a post at the University of Cape Town in 1923.
A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, Huard studied under Georges-Jean Pinault and is attested in 2026 as an Assistent at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
